claims.claim: Tabletop Sentinel's writer says the curated AI-produced designer bios read as AI-generated work.
claims.quote: they not only read as AI generated work

claims.claim: An EN World poster presents a ChatGPT essay on generic RPG campaign settings as an instance where the model shows the limits of neural network text generation.
claims.quote: Sometimes it shows the limits of neural network text generation.

claims.claim: The One-Page RPG Jam 2025's generative-AI policy forbids text generated from a prompt and also text merely re-written by a generative AI tool.
claims.source: Unknown Dungeon (jam host), itch.io community policy
claims.quote: use text generated from a prompt in your game

claims.claim: Reviewing 'Three Witches', a product whose DriveThruRPG description is labelled as containing AI-generated content, Bryce Lynch writes that nothing in its hex crawl is specific.
claims.source: Bryce Lynch, tenfootpole.org review of 'Three Witches' by Rutibex
claims.quote: There’s nothing specific about anything in that fucking hex crawl.
claims.page: review body, on the hex descriptions

claims.claim: Bryce Lynch describes the typical hex entry in that product as a one-liner about the terrain followed by a list of things the party might encounter.
claims.source: Bryce Lynch, tenfootpole.org review of 'Three Witches'
claims.quote: A little one liner that is super generic about the terrain
claims.page: review body, on the hex descriptions

claims.claim: He objects that the DM-facing line states the room's intended effect instead of designing a room that produces it, telling the DM that the entrance is a foreboding entrance.
claims.source: Bryce Lynch, tenfootpole.org review of 'Three Witches'
claims.quote: telling the DM that this is a foreboding entrance
claims.page: review body, on the dungeon rooms

claims.claim: Compton names the failure of a generator whose outputs are mathematically unique but perceived as all alike the 10,000 Bowls of Oatmeal problem.
claims.source: Kate Compton, 'So you want to build a generator...', galaxykate0.tumblr.com, 22 Feb 2016
claims.quote: But the user will likely just see a lot of oatmeal

claims.feature: other: perceptual uniqueness as the metric
claims.claim: Compton asserts that perceptual uniqueness, not mathematical uniqueness, is the real metric for a generator's output.
claims.source: Kate Compton, 'So you want to build a generator...', galaxykate0.tumblr.com, 22 Feb 2016
claims.quote: Perceptual uniqueness is the real metric

claims.claim: Compton distinguishes perceptual differentiation, the feeling that a piece of content is not identical to the previous one, as an easier bar than perceptual uniqueness.
claims.source: Kate Compton, 'So you want to build a generator...', galaxykate0.tumblr.com, 22 Feb 2016
claims.quote: the feeling that this piece of content is not identical

claims.claim: Compton says a reader glancing at a line of trees can tell when they are less varied than expected, which reads as unnaturalness.
claims.source: Kate Compton, 'So you want to build a generator...', galaxykate0.tumblr.com, 22 Feb 2016

claims.claim: Compton says parametric methods, which vary an existing artifact along fixed numerical paths, can produce something new but never something surprising.
claims.source: Kate Compton, 'So you want to build a generator...', galaxykate0.tumblr.com, 22 Feb 2016

claims.feature: other: distribution methods fail on language
claims.claim: Compton says randomly selected strings of words do not have enough structure to make interesting meaning.
claims.source: Kate Compton, 'So you want to build a generator...', galaxykate0.tumblr.com, 22 Feb 2016
claims.quote: enough structure to make interesting meaning

claims.claim: Compton says grammars do not have a way to handle constraints unless the constraints are implicitly encoded in the grammar itself.
claims.source: Kate Compton, 'So you want to build a generator...', galaxykate0.tumblr.com, 22 Feb 2016
claims.quote: they do not have a way to handle constraints

claims.claim: Compton says restricting a generator to be more conservative in its choices may lose interesting possibility space.
claims.source: Kate Compton, 'So you want to build a generator...', galaxykate0.tumblr.com, 22 Feb 2016
claims.quote: though that may lose interesting possibility space

claims.feature: other: evidence of process as character
claims.claim: Compton says humans seem to like perceiving evidence of process and forces in a generated artifact.
claims.source: Kate Compton, 'So you want to build a generator...', galaxykate0.tumblr.com, 22 Feb 2016
claims.quote: Humans seem to like perceiving evidence of process and forces
